title: Built an AI Gaming Presence. The hardest part wasn’t making her talk. It was making her timing feel natural.
author: SubzeroSun
selftext:
I’ve spent 11 months building Monday, an AI Presence for my gaming sessions. I wanted someone who could follow what I’m doing and talk some shit with me without needing me to stop playing and type everything out.



She’s not an NPC inside the game, and she doesn’t play for me. She observes the stream’s live visuals and talks with me while I game(and workout between rounds). I’m sharing the development side because the problems overlap with voiced NPCs and companions: knowing what’s happening, deciding whether it’s worth saying, and not delivering the right line after the moment has already passed.



I’ve used ChatGPT, Claude and Codex throughout the build. My loop has become: play a real session, preserve the footage and logs, compare what she actually said with what was on screen, then work through the failures. Passing tests and having a good experience in the chair have not always been the same thing.



Some of the hiccups:

\- She can land a natural callback, then get repetitive about the score.

\- A reply can be relevant but arrive when I’m already reacting to something else.

\- During a movement break she acknowledged missing my shadowboxing, then walked that acknowledgment back.

\- In another break she named goblet squats after I asked, then mentioned the ab wheel without another immediate question. Her voice was choppy there even though the recognition was useful.

That’s why I’m keeping the rough parts in the evidence instead of only showing the ten seconds where she looks brilliant. I’m documenting it through my PhoenixFlock channel, where the sessions combine gaming, conversation and short workouts between matches.



For people building voiced characters or companions: how do you test whether a line is still worth saying by the time the player hears it? Do you replay the same moment with different delays, or judge it another way? I’m especially interested in where you choose silence over a late response.



Here’s a continuous 28:20 excerpt on my own channel, including gameplay, failed transitions and movement breaks: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PfzFf85Fu3A. It contains Gears combat and strong language. This footage is from before the latest repair work, not proof that those problems are fixed.
